criteria: `LRUCache` in `cache.py`: `LRUCache(capacity)` holds at most `capacity` entries. When `put` adds a new key to a full cache, the least recently used entry is dropped first. An entry is used when it is put and when it is read with `get`.

`LRUCache.get(key, default=None)` returns the stored value and counts as a use: with capacity 2, after `put("a", 1)`, `put("b", 2)`, `get("a")` and `put("c", 3)` the cache holds `a` and `c` and has dropped `b`.
`LRUCache.get` of a key that is not in the cache returns `default`. It stores nothing and changes no order.
`LRUCache.put` of a key that is already in the cache replaces its value and counts as a use. Nothing is dropped, even when the cache is full.
For an `LRUCache`, `key in cache` and `len(cache)` do not count as a use.
`LRUCache` has a new method `keys()` that returns the keys as a list, from the least recently used to the most recently used. Calling `keys()` does not count as a use.
`LRUCache` can store any value, `None` included: when the stored value is `None`, `get` returns the stored `None` and not `default`, and the entry stays in the cache.
Creating an `LRUCache` with a `capacity` below 1 raises `ValueError` when the cache is created.
The provided tests in test_visible.py pass, with that file unchanged
